title: Cross-platform browser tests
lede: The task requires Chrome (Windows and Mac), Firefox (all platforms) and Edge. CI used to run the browser tests only in Chromium and Firefox on Linux. PRs now also run them in the real Chrome, Edge and Firefox builds on Windows and macOS, without making the other checks slower.

files.question: Which browsers do the browser tests run in?
files.summary: Reads a comma-separated `BROWSERS` list, defaulting to Chromium and Firefox.
files.owns: Mapping a browser name to a Vitest browser instance, including the branded Chrome and Edge builds.
files.never: Knows which OS it runs on.
files.tested: Run locally with `BROWSERS=chrome,firefox` (26 passed) and with an unknown name (fails loudly).

files.question: Where and when does each browser run?
files.summary: Adds a PR-only `cross-browser` matrix over Windows and macOS, and cancels outdated PR runs.
files.owns: Which browsers each OS runs, browser caching, and run cancellation.
files.never: Repeats the checks that don't depend on the OS.

scenarios.name: A PR runs the Windows job

steps.title: Only PRs start the matrix
steps.explain: The matrix is skipped on pushes to `main`: the PR already tested the same code, and the Linux `check` job still guards every deploy. `fail-fast: false` lets a Windows failure not hide a macOS one.

steps.title: Each OS picks its browsers
steps.explain: Windows runs all three required browsers. macOS runs Chrome and Firefox, the two the task names for Mac. Both jobs run in parallel, so the wait is the slower of the two, not the sum.

steps.title: Only Firefox is downloaded, and it is cached
steps.explain: GitHub's runners already have Chrome and Edge. Firefox goes into a folder in the workspace, cached by OS and Playwright version, so a version bump downloads it again and nothing else does. `.playwright-browsers/` is git-ignored.

steps.title: Only the browser tests run
steps.explain: Typecheck, lint, coverage, build and the walkthrough check give the same answer on any OS, so they run once, in `check`. The job passes its browser list to the tests through `BROWSERS`.

steps.title: The config turns names into browser instances
steps.explain: `chromium` and `firefox` are Playwright's own builds. `chrome` and `msedge` are the installed branded browsers, launched through Playwright's Chromium with a `channel`, each with its own provider and a `name` so the report tells them apart. Without `BROWSERS`, local runs and the Linux job behave exactly as before.

steps.title: The run fails instead of testing nothing
steps.explain: An unknown name throws with the list of valid names. Run locally: `BROWSERS=bogus` fails with `unknown browser "bogus"`. Silently skipping it would make a job pass while testing fewer browsers than it claims.

scenarios.name: A second push to the same PR

steps.title: The outdated run is cancelled
steps.explain: Runs share a group per ref. Only PR runs cancel each other: a push to `main` is never cancelled, so every merge deploys.

notes.title: The new jobs are not required yet
notes.detail: The ruleset requires only `check`. Until `cross-browser (windows-latest, …)` and `cross-browser (macos-latest, …)` are added as required checks, a failing one won't block merging. They can only be added after they have run once.

notes.title: Edge was not run locally
notes.detail: This Mac has no Edge, so `msedge` failed to launch here. Chrome and Firefox passed locally; Edge is first proven by this PR's Windows job.

notes.title: Linux keeps Chromium, not branded Chrome
notes.detail: The `check` job is unchanged. Branded Chrome on Linux would add little: the task names Chrome on Windows and Mac, which the matrix now covers.
